- [2023/05/21] The study involved manipulating the mode of color presentation in two conditions: color combined with target shape or color shown separately on a ring.
- [2023/05/21] The color match between memory and saccadic choice display was manipulated in three conditions: target-match, distractor-match, and no-match.
- [2023/05/21] Participants completed 384 trials, with each mode of color presentation having 96 trials in the no-match condition, and 48 trials each in the target- and distractor-match conditions.
- [2023/05/21] 15.8% of trials were removed due to errors such as anticipations, late trials, imprecise initial fixations, delayed initial fixations, and amplitude errors.
- [2023/05/21] More correct responses occurred when the target in the choice display matched the color from the memory display, and fewer correct responses occurred when the distractor matched the color.
- [2023/05/21] The effect of color match was weaker when color and shape were presented separately.
- [2023/05/21] Individual median saccadic reaction times were shorter in the target-match condition compared to the distractor-match and no-match conditions.
- [2023/05/21] The study suggests that attentional guidance by irrelevant color features was reduced when separated from the relevant target shape, possibly due to reduced encoding of color into working memory.
